Internal helper: a variable named in quotes inside a formula

Source: R/checks.R
dot-jst_formula_quoted_stop.Rd

jt(Score ~ "Gender", d) printed its title and stopped on R's "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed"; jlm(Score ~ Age + "Region", d) on "invalid model formula in ExtractVars"; the plot form said NA was not found (ruling R18, Session 355; built Session 356). A string standing as a term – an operand of the formula's own operators, ~ + - * : / | ^ and parentheses – is the sibling of "The formula should not be in quotes": the stop names the first such term and gives the call as typed with every quoted term's quotes removed. A string inside a computed term (I(Source == "web")) is R code and is left alone.

Usage

.jst_formula_quoted_stop(formula, cl, fn)

Arguments

formula

The formula.

cl

The call as typed, for the line.

fn

Character(1); the user-facing function's name.

Value

Invisible NULL; stops when a quoted term is found.
